biophysical_burden.boundary: Significantly decreased-flow basin inventory; no cause or storage response is assigned.

human_economic_burden.boundary: Resident exposure, not a count of measured household shortages or economic losses.

source_locators: UN-Water 2024 update: one or more water-related ecosystem types are degraded in 50 percent of countries, more than 90 of 185 reporting countries.
UN-Water 2024 report: freshwater species populations have declined globally by 83 percent since 1970.
UN-Water 2024 update: river flow significantly decreased in 402 of 12,572 basins, a fivefold increase from 15 years earlier, with 107.5 million people living in those basins.
UN-Water 2024 update: permanent surface water receded in 364 of 13,894 basins, where 93.1 million people live.
excluded_from_scoring: the sum of potentially overlapping reduced-flow and receding-water populations
unreported ecosystems treated as stable or degraded

transformations.formula: Normalize the source-reported fivefold increase in significantly decreased-flow basins.
Normalize resident population in affected basins without relabeling exposure as shortage.
Divide affected basins by assessed basins; do not treat unassessed basins as unaffected.

receipts.uncertainty: Country reporting, satellite coverage, basin delineation, trend significance, observation epochs, monitoring density and national indicator composition vary. A country is counted degraded when at least one included ecosystem type is degraded; this does not mean every freshwater ecosystem in that country is degraded.
receipts.freshness: UNEP and UN-Water SDG 6.6.1 assessment 2024; snapshot captured 2026-07-31T21:47:06.642Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: UN-Water quantifies the accumulated global reduced-inflow basin inventory, exposed population, 15-year comparison and assessed-basin extent.
higher_priority_failures: The USGS operational source is station- and US-bounded and cannot provide a current global aggregation.
The global assessment does not provide a complete 20-year annual observation panel, so it remains accumulated impact.
